characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Galadriel is a high elf of immense wisdom, telepathic power, and ancient might who fights primarily using mind-control, magical protection, and subtle mental influence rather than direct physical combat.

techniques: Banishment of shadow and destruction of fortress walls

mechanisms: Elven ring Nenya granting preservation and concealment
Immense personal spiritual power shielding her mind

weaknesses: Vulnerable to moral temptation by the One Ring
Bound by the physical limitations of an elven physical form
limitations: Power wanes as the Third Age ends and the Elves diminish

sources.supports: General attributes, role in Middle-earth, and use of Nenya.

feats.claim: Pulled down the walls of Dol Guldur during the War of the Ring.
feats.citation: The Fellowship of the Ring / Appendix B

notableResults.citation: History of Middle-earth / The Silmarillion context
notableResults.note: Resisted his influence and aided in dismantling his strongholds.

conditional.ability: Destruction of Dol Guldur's walls and banishment of evil presence
conditional.dependsOn: Her presence in Middle-earth backed by her ring Nenya

campaignTags.claim: Wields the power of Nenya and ancient elven magic.
Reads and communicates through minds across great distances.

unknowns: Exact limits of her power when directly engaging in physical warfare

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Gandalf is a Maia spirit incarnated as an old wizard who relies on staff-work, light-based magic, fire-making, and inspirational leadership, frequently avoiding direct combat in favor of tactical support.

mechanisms: Durable physical form as an Istari

weaknesses: Restricted by the Valar from matching Sauron in raw might
Physical body subject to exhaustion and trauma
limitations: Forbidden by the Valar to contend with Sauron with equal force
Prone to physical weariness in his elderly wizard guise

sources.supports: General profile, status as a Maia, and magical capabilities.

feats.claim: Fought the Balrog of Moria for days before defeating it.

notableResults.note: Resulted in the death of Gandalf's physical grey form.

conditional.ability: Resistance to fatigue and inspiring courage in followers
conditional.dependsOn: Carrying the Ring of Fire, Narya

campaignTags.claim: Produces fire and light via spells and the ring Narya.

unknowns: Full extent of his power when not constrained by his Istari form

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Gandalf the White possesses vastly increased authority, radiance, and power compared to his Grey form, allowing him to break spells, shatter weapons, and command armies with absolute confidence.

mechanisms: Radiant aura that deflects magical assault

weaknesses: Still bound to human-like physical endurance within his incarnate body
characters.formDifferences: Replaces Gandalf the Grey with heightened spiritual power, authority over other Maiar, and a radiant white robe and aura.

sources.supports: Transition to Gandalf the White and enhanced status.

notableResults.note: Confronted at the gates of Minas Tirith before the battle was interrupted.

unknowns: Exact mechanics of his resurrection and promotion by Eru Ilúvatar

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Legendarium / Silmarillion)
characters.summary: Olórin in his uncloaked angelic state is a pure Maia spirit of Valinor, possessing formless or radiant spiritual might, wisdom, and pity without the physical limitations of an old man.
weaknesses: Cannot directly dominate free peoples by force
characters.formDifferences: Represents his primordial form as a Maia in Valinor prior to taking flesh as an Istari.

sources.supports: Description of Olórin as a Maia in Valinor before his mission.

unknowns: Direct combat feats in uncloaked form prior to incarnation

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Gil-galad was the last High King of the Noldor in Middle-earth, fighting with elite elven martial skill and wielding the legendary spear Aeglos.
weaknesses: Vulnerable to extreme heat and physical trauma
limitations: Limited to mortal physical endurance despite elven longevity

sources.supports: Role as High King of the Noldor and combat during the Last Alliance.

feats.claim: Fought alongside Elendil against Sauron on the slopes of Orodruin.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion / Fellowship of the Ring

notableResults.note: Perished in combat alongside Elendil while defeating Sauron's physical form.

conditional.ability: Piercing enemy ranks with devastating efficiency

unknowns: Exact details of single combat exchanges against Sauron

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Gimli is a stout Dwarf warrior who fights with heavy axes, unmatched physical endurance, and immense courage in close-quarters melee combat.

mechanisms: Dwarven resilience against fatigue and injury

weaknesses: Limited mobility in open or water terrain due to heavy armor
Short physical reach compared to larger foes
limitations: Cannot engage targets at range effectively without thrown axes

sources.supports: Character profile, weapon usage, and role in battles.

feats.claim: Slew numerous orcs at the Battle of Helm's Deep and the Pelennor Fields.
feats.citation: The Two Towers / The Return of the King

notableResults.note: Defeated numerous Uruk-hai during the defense of Helm's Deep.

unknowns: Performance against giant or magical combatants without aid

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (The Silmarillion / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Glaurung is the Father of Dragons, a massive wingless reptile who attacks with crushing physical weight, intense dragon-fire, and powerful hypnotic psychological domination.

techniques: Hypnotic gaze causing memory loss and despair

mechanisms: Impenetrable scaled hide protecting against conventional weapons

weaknesses: Soft underbelly vulnerable to deep thrusts from powerful blades
limitations: Lacks wings, restricting him to ground travel

sources.supports: Characteristics as the first dragon, fire-breathing, and hypnotic gaze.

feats.claim: Devastated Nargothrond and manipulated Túrin Turambar through psychological deceit.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion / The Children of Húrin

notableResults.note: Slain by Túrin from beneath with the black sword Gurthang, though Glaurung successfully ruined Túrin's life beforehand.

campaignTags.claim: Enormous dragon of colossal physical proportions.

unknowns: Exact resistance to high-tier divine magic

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Glorfindel is a mighty Elf-lord of Rivendell with near-demigod status, possessing immense martial prowess, swiftness, and spiritual terror that drives back Nazgûl.

mechanisms: Resilience bridging the seen and unseen worlds

weaknesses: Physical form can still be slain by powerful enough entities, as shown in his past death against a Balrog
limitations: Cannot be everywhere at once across Middle-earth

sources.supports: Profile as a powerful Elf-lord reborn with near-Maiar strength.

feats.claim: Slew a Balrog in single combat during the Fall of Gondolin.
feats.citation: The Silmarillion / The Fellowship of the Ring

notableResults.note: Glorfindel died in the process of dragging the Balrog down into an abyss.

campaignTags.claim: Possesses potent elven spiritual presence capable of repelling Nazgûl.

unknowns: Full extent of his power in Third Age conflicts compared to his First Age peak

weaknesses: Physically fragile and easily overpowered in direct fair fights
Vulnerable to bright sunlight and elven rope
limitations: Weak physical strength against armed opponents

sources.supports: Character traits, physical abilities, and cave survival skills.

feats.claim: Stangled Déagol to claim the One Ring.

notableResults.note: Ambushed and murdered him over the Ring.

conditional.dependsOn: Possession and wearing of the One Ring

campaignTags.claim: Hides and moves unseen in darkness and shadows.
Expert swimmer in subterranean waters and lakes.

unknowns: Combat effectiveness away from rocky or dark environments

characters.continuity: The Lord of the Rings (Books / Legendarium)
characters.summary: Sméagol before the corruption of the One Ring was a normal river-folk hobbit-like creature leading a peaceful community life, possessing no notable combat training.
weaknesses: No combat experience or defensive training
characters.formDifferences: Represents Sméagol prior to his corruption, featuring normal hobbit-like stature, sanity, and river-dwelling habits without monstrous agility or malice.
